A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MoMoE research. Their complete text, figures, tables and Appendices A–H are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original moderation experiments, explanation validation, expert/operator analyses, and class-imbalance experiments in Appendix G.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds a manual analysis of 100 incorrect moderation decisions.

M1.justification: The four operators, expert models, LoRA training, allocation and aggregation procedures, and GPT-4o explanation generation remain unchanged. The softmax wording is clarified; proposed prosocial experts appear only as future work.

E1.justification: Both evaluate Reddit comment moderation using the same seven source and 30 target communities, including the same class-imbalance scenarios. The new r/movies error audit examines an existing target community rather than extending task or dataset coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same methods: GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini, base and fine-tuned Llama/Mistral models, global SLMs, and Detoxify. Appendix G retains the same global-SLM comparators.

E3.justification: New Section 6 introduces an audit protocol: sample 50 false positives and 50 false negatives from Mistral-based MoMoECommunity on r/movies, using classification allocation and majority voting, then open-code the errors. Existing experimental settings remain unchanged; Table 1's added configuration description is disclosure.

E4.justification: v2 adds a focused error analysis identifying failure categories among 100 r/movies predictions. Existing expert-count, operator, precision-recall and class-imbalance analyses are retained. This is a limited supplementary investigation of one community and configuration.

E5.justification: Welch's tests, significance annotations, variability reporting, annotation agreement, and Appendix G's ten random seeds with mean and standard deviation are retained. The new error-category counts do not introduce uncertainty estimation or repeated-run reporting.

E6.justification: New Table 2 reports error-category counts, including 16 sarcasm/joke cases among 50 false positives and 12 off-topic cases among 50 false negatives. Existing benchmark values and plotted findings remain unchanged, including v1 Table 2, renumbered Table 3 in v2.

T1.justification: The mathematical descriptions of similarity, softmax allocation and weighted aggregation retain their meaning. Neither version introduces additional formal assumptions, propositions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims: modular cross-community moderation, reliable trace-based explanations, and best Micro-F1 scores of 0.72 and 0.67. The added audit does not redefine these central claims.

C2.justification: Section 6 adds interpretations of over-flagged humor/civil criticism and missed subtle toxicity or contextual norm violations, motivating stronger contextual reasoning. Section 8 expands future directions for human-outcome evaluation and prosocial moderation. Existing limitations remain.

D1.justification: Table 1 newly specifies classification-based allocation and dot-product aggregation for its reported models. The first-page footnote replaces a promised code/model release with a direct code pointer under scuba-illinois. Appendix training details, prompts and compute disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: The future-work discussion adds five works on prosocial discourse and positive reinforcement: Bao et al. (2021), Grimmelmann (2015), Goyal et al. (2025), and Lambert et al. (2024, 2025). Core positioning remains unchanged; Park et al. (2022) receives a publication-metadata update.

P1.justification: v2 standardizes source/target terminology in several passages, clarifies allocation wording, edits related-work and discussion prose, and inserts an error-analysis section and future-work paragraphs. The overall narrative and most existing text remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the error-taxonomy table and moves Table 1's expanded caption below the table. Existing figures retain their visual content; the imbalanced-results table is renumbered and retained. Other layout changes mainly involve spacing and pagination.

improvement.justification: The new error audit provides concrete failure categories beyond v1's aggregate performance and precision-recall analyses. The clarified Table 1 configuration and updated code pointer also improve reporting. These gains are limited: the audit covers one community and configuration, while benchmark evidence and the acknowledged absence of user-centered evaluation remain unchanged.
